name: Tabs
summary: Use Tabs to let experienced users switch between closely related sections of content without leaving the page.
whenToUse: Use for users who are familiar with tabbed interfaces, such as caseworkers switching between related data views.
Use only when users do not need to compare the sections at the same time.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for primary page or site navigation, or to hide steps in a journey.
Do not use when users need to read sections in order or compare information across them.

anatomy.name: Tabs module
anatomy.description: The root contains a fallback contents heading, link list and corresponding panels.

anatomy.name: Tab links
anatomy.description: Each ordinary anchor targets the id of one content panel.

anatomy.name: Panels
anatomy.description: Each uniquely identified panel contains a heading and its complete content.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: Two or more closely related content views for experienced users.

behaviour: Initialise govuk-tabs so wide screens receive tab semantics, keyboard behaviour and history-fragment updates.
On narrow screens and without JavaScript, links and panels behave as an in-page table of contents rather than an inaccessible tab widget.
Do not manually add ARIA tab roles; allow the official GOV.UK module to enhance the base markup.
accessibility: Every tab href must match one unique panel id and every panel needs a descriptive heading.
Keep all content in the document so it remains reachable before enhancement.
Test keyboard navigation, back and forward navigation, and layouts at high zoom.
content: Use short, distinct tab labels that describe the panel content.
Keep the number of tabs small enough to remain understandable and usable on narrow screens.
Do not repeat the same information in multiple panels.
